findings.text: Split at the limit is changed by the save. Steps: scale page 1 (S0); Add flashing → New flashing → Details → Lengths; Run tool: tap (5,000, 1,000) → (11,000, 1,000) → (11,000, 5,000) (= 10,000 mm); tap the red part → "Split at the limit (8,800 mm along the run). Pieces now 9,000 + 1,400 mm"; Finish → after "Saved" the sheet reads: "Finished — one run: Measured 10,000 along the run → 2 pieces, each with its own 200 allowance: Piece 1: 8,800.02 + 200 → 9,100 mm — over the maximum Piece 2: 1,200 + 200 …" and still says "tap it to split at the limit (8,800 mm along the run)" (src/components/takeoff/measure/PathPanel.jsx:60) although the run is already split there. The server now computes 1 × 9100 (ceiling_exceeded,split_invalid) / 1 × 3200 / 1 × 1400 (ceiling_exceeded,split_invalid), and the order is blocked ("A piece is longer than the order ceiling…", "The split pieces do not cover the run."). Cause: server/lib/takeoff/takeoffService.mjs:242 cleans inputs.splitAnchors x/y — PDF-point coordinates — with MM() (:204-208, Math.round(n * 1000) / 1000): stored [{"x":431.811,"y":257.717,"stationMm":8800}] vs the app's [{"stationMm":8800,"x":431.8110236220473,"y":257.7165354330707}]; shared/takeoff/engine/flashingPath.js:298 (checkSplits → locateOnPath) then rebuilds the station from the rounded anchor (8,800 → 8,800.02 → 9,000.02 → 9,100). Real-engine cross-check on the server's own snapshot: stored anchor → 1x1400(ceiling_exceeded,split_invalid) 1x3200 1x9100(ceiling_exceeded,split_invalid); full-precision anchor → 1x1400 1x3200 1x9000; no anchor → 1x1400 1x3200 1x9000. Rounding the other way would instead silently make piece 2 1,500 (any split at a whole-mm station is exposed).

Site appendix provenance is wrong for walls entered by numbers: server/lib/takeoff/takeoffPdf.mjs:214 hard-codes "· Derived from plan + entered heights" on every wall setout. The North wall was typed in (Walls → Wall by numbers); the wall editor labels it "Entered" and the schedule "Entered length and heights". Steps: J2 (wall by numbers) → Orders → export → Site appendix (cutting & setout).

Site appendix prints a literal "?" for "≥": "shortest listed length ? its cut …". The cladding explanation (shared/takeoff/engine/cladding.js:566) goes through winAnsi() (server/lib/takeoff/takeoffPdf.mjs:28-35), which maps only "→"; every other non-WinAnsi character becomes "?". Steps: J2 → Orders → export → Site appendix.

Site appendix timber cut list names the rafters out of station order and only the first 12: "Rafter @ 0, Rafter @ 10,000, Rafter @ 1,200, Rafter @ 1,800, Rafter @ 2,400, Rafter @ 3,000, Rafter @ 3,600, Rafter @ 4,200, Rafter @ 4,800, Rafter @ … +6 more" — so a site reader can't tell which stations the 6 unnamed ones are. Labels are collected in the allocator's cut order (shared/takeoff/engine/dispatch.js:369-380; equal lengths tie-break on cut-id text: byLengthDesc, shared/takeoff/engine/allocator.js:512) and truncated at 12 (server/lib/takeoff/takeoffPdf.mjs:208). Steps: J1 → Orders → export → Site appendix.
